chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that they asked him:

about the meat of domestic donkeys, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating it on the day of Khaybar, and he only forbade eating it at that time because they were the beasts of burden of the people, and indeed, the forbidden is only that which Allah, Exalted and Glorious, has forbidden in the Quran.

key_terms.حَمُولَةَ النَّاسِ: beasts of burden of the people

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet forbid eating domestic donkeys only during the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the prohibition on domestic donkeys was a temporary ruling specific to the Battle of Khaybar, where they served as essential beasts of burden, rather than a permanent dietary ban. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly principle that only what is explicitly declared haram in the Quran is eternally forbidden, whereas other prohibitions may be abrogated or contextual. This hadith is central to the debate between the Akhbari and Usuli schools regarding the scope of the Prophet's authority to institute temporary prohibitions.
